title: Why static methods are used
answer: Use a static method when the operation conceptually belongs to the class or utility and does not require per-object state. Static methods are common for pure calculations, factories, validators, and helper operations. AeroTopo's `SurveyAlgorithms` methods are static because calls such as `unique`, `mergeSorted`, and `binarySearch` operate entirely on supplied arguments and maintain no SurveyAlgorithms instance state. If behavior needs object-specific configuration or mutable state, an instance method is usually more appropriate.
